key_insight: Multi-task active learning works better when conflict, informativeness, and diversity are treated as separate design problems instead of a single weighted score.
engineering_relevance: This framework can improve annotation efficiency in multi-task perception systems by selecting more useful samples while avoiding noisy diversity and misleading conflict penalties.
method: Do not score gradient conflict in acquisition; resolve training interference with gradient surgery.
Use orthogonal decomposition: first filter for informativeness, then maximize coverage/diversity.
Estimate cross-task mutual information from MC-dropout task entropies to capture task dependency.
evidence_signal: Experiments on COCO, Cityscapes, and NYUv2 against recent MTL-AL and data-selection baselines show consistent gains over state-of-the-art methods.
watch_item: CTMI depends on MC-dropout entropy estimates and the two-stage selection pipeline, so performance may be sensitive to uncertainty calibration and implementation details.
paper_title: Deconstructing Multi-Task Active Learning: The Paradox of Gradient Conflict and Orthogonal Decomposition
